report.scope: Complete repeated solves with ordinary formatted output or a shared external checksum consumer. The sink removes output-list construction and formatting in fwp, and formatting in C/Rust, but adds checksum work. This difference is not pure output time or pure arithmetic time. Arithmetic, input creation, update buffers, bounds checks and cleanup remain. No LTO; the same separately compiled C consumer reads every result coordinate. Compilation, dump validation, memory profiles and RSS probes are excluded from timed samples. C/Rust reuse two numerical buffers; fwp constructs immutable arrays. Memory profiles cover fwp managed/raw storage and only the numerical buffers in C/Rust; those scopes are not directly comparable. Instrumentation can prevent allocation elimination, so its counts are not an allocation trace of the timed executable. Process RSS covers each complete process. One run does not establish a compiler speed improvement.

measurements.scope: Independent inspection of 109 measurement/control executables and 60 untimed native controls. Timing conclusions require separate control and repeated-run analysis.

report.scope: Complete repeated solves with ordinary formatted output or a shared external checksum consumer. The sink removes output-list construction and formatting in fwp, and formatting in C/Rust, but adds checksum work. This difference is not pure output time or pure arithmetic time. Arithmetic, input creation, update buffers, bounds checks and cleanup remain. No LTO; the same separately compiled C consumer reads every result coordinate. Compilation, dump validation, memory profiles and RSS probes are excluded from timed samples. C/Rust reuse two numerical buffers; fwp constructs immutable arrays. Memory profiles cover fwp managed/raw storage and only the numerical buffers in C/Rust; those scopes are not directly comparable. Instrumentation can prevent allocation elimination, so its counts are not an allocation trace of the timed executable. Process RSS covers each complete process. One run does not establish a compiler speed improvement.

measurements.scope: Independent inspection of 109 measurement/control executables and 60 untimed native controls. Timing conclusions require separate control and repeated-run analysis.

report.scope: Complete repeated solves with ordinary formatted output or a shared external checksum consumer. The sink removes output-list construction and formatting in fwp, and formatting in C/Rust, but adds checksum work. This difference is not pure output time or pure arithmetic time. Arithmetic, input creation, update buffers, bounds checks and cleanup remain. No LTO; the same separately compiled C consumer reads every result coordinate. Compilation, dump validation, memory profiles and RSS probes are excluded from timed samples. Each compiler command has a separate explicit deadline and recorded wall time; build-commands.json is updated after each attempt, including failures. These wall times include host scheduling delays. C/Rust reuse two numerical buffers; fwp constructs immutable arrays. Memory profiles cover fwp managed/raw storage and only the numerical buffers in C/Rust; those scopes are not directly comparable. Instrumentation can prevent allocation elimination, so its counts are not an allocation trace of the timed executable. Process RSS covers each complete process. One run does not establish a compiler speed improvement.

measurements.scope: Independent inspection of 109 measurement/control executables and 60 untimed native controls. Timing conclusions require separate control and repeated-run analysis.

report.scope: Complete repeated solves with ordinary formatted output or a shared external checksum consumer. The sink removes output-list construction and formatting in fwp, and formatting in C/Rust, but adds checksum work. This difference is not pure output time or pure arithmetic time. Arithmetic, input creation, update buffers, bounds checks and cleanup remain. No LTO; the same separately compiled C consumer reads every result coordinate. Compilation, dump validation, memory profiles and RSS probes are excluded from timed samples. Each compiler command has a separate explicit deadline and recorded wall time; build-commands.json is updated after each attempt, including failures. These wall times include host scheduling delays. C/Rust reuse two numerical buffers; fwp constructs immutable arrays. Memory profiles cover fwp managed/raw storage and only the numerical buffers in C/Rust; those scopes are not directly comparable. Instrumentation can prevent allocation elimination, so its counts are not an allocation trace of the timed executable. Process RSS covers each complete process. One run does not establish a compiler speed improvement.

measurements.scope: Independent inspection of 109 measurement/control executables and 60 untimed native controls. Timing conclusions require separate control and repeated-run analysis.

report.scope: Complete repeated solves with ordinary formatted output or a shared external checksum consumer. Full-output fwp formats the numeric array directly; neither fwp mode creates an output list. The sink replaces formatted output with checksum work in all three implementations. This difference is not pure output time or pure arithmetic time. Arithmetic, input creation, update buffers, bounds checks and cleanup remain. No LTO; the same separately compiled C consumer reads every result coordinate. Compilation, dump validation, memory profiles and RSS probes are excluded from timed samples. Each compiler command has a separate explicit deadline and recorded wall time; build-commands.json is updated after each attempt, including failures. These wall times include host scheduling delays. C/Rust reuse two numerical buffers; fwp constructs immutable arrays. Memory profiles cover fwp managed/raw storage and only the numerical buffers in C/Rust; those scopes are not directly comparable. Instrumentation can prevent allocation elimination, so its counts are not an allocation trace of the timed executable. Process RSS covers each complete process. One run does not establish a compiler speed improvement.

measurements.scope: Independent inspection of 109 measurement/control executables and 60 untimed native controls. Timing conclusions require separate control and repeated-run analysis.

report.scope: Complete repeated solves with ordinary formatted output or a shared external checksum consumer. Full-output fwp formats the numeric array directly; neither fwp mode creates an output list. The sink replaces formatted output with checksum work in all three implementations. This difference is not pure output time or pure arithmetic time. Arithmetic, input creation, update buffers, bounds checks and cleanup remain. No LTO; the same separately compiled C consumer reads every result coordinate. Compilation, dump validation, memory profiles and RSS probes are excluded from timed samples. Each compiler command has a separate explicit deadline and recorded wall time; build-commands.json is updated after each attempt, including failures. These wall times include host scheduling delays. C/Rust reuse two numerical buffers; fwp constructs immutable arrays. Memory profiles cover fwp managed/raw storage and only the numerical buffers in C/Rust; those scopes are not directly comparable. Instrumentation can prevent allocation elimination, so its counts are not an allocation trace of the timed executable. Process RSS covers each complete process. One run does not establish a compiler speed improvement.

measurements.scope: Independent inspection of 109 measurement/control executables and 60 untimed native controls. Timing conclusions require separate control and repeated-run analysis.

report.scope: Complete repeated solves with ordinary formatted output or a shared external checksum consumer. The sink removes output-list construction and formatting in fwp, and formatting in C/Rust, but adds checksum work. This difference is not pure output time or pure arithmetic time. Arithmetic, input creation, update buffers, bounds checks and cleanup remain. No LTO; the same separately compiled C consumer reads every result coordinate. Compilation, dump validation, memory profiles and RSS probes are excluded from timed samples. C/Rust reuse two numerical buffers; fwp constructs immutable arrays. Memory profiles cover fwp managed/raw storage and only the numerical buffers in C/Rust; those scopes are not directly comparable. Instrumentation can prevent allocation elimination, so its counts are not an allocation trace of the timed executable. Process RSS covers each complete process. One run does not establish a compiler speed improvement.

measurements.scope: Independent inspection of 109 measurement/control executables and 60 untimed native controls. Timing conclusions require separate control and repeated-run analysis.
